items.headline: Saudi-backed Yemeni government launches full offensive to retake Houthi territory, including Bab al-Mandeb Strait
items.summary: Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council chairman announced a military campaign to retake Houthi-held Sanaa and the Bab al-Mandeb shipping chokepoint. Coalition forces conducted 257 strikes Saturday Oct 3 plus 97 more Sunday Oct 4; Houthis claimed retaliatory strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities. The US said it will not take kinetic action "for now."
items.actionable: Escalation at a second Red Sea/Gulf chokepoint (Bab al-Mandeb) alongside Hormuz reinforces the safe-haven case for GLD/SLV and the large cash pile's optionality; watch shipping/freight-rate pass-through risk.

items.headline: Explosions reported in the Strait of Hormuz; initial reports of missiles fired at transiting ships
items.summary: Explosions were heard in the Strait of Hormuz area Sunday evening Oct 4, with initial reporting suggesting missiles fired from Iran at ships in transit. This follows a week of tanker incidents in the strait and comes as a second front (Yemen/Bab al-Mandeb) opens simultaneously.
items.actionable: Direct hit to the Hormuz transit risk already underpinning Brent/WTI and gold/silver's safe-haven bid -- reinforces not reducing precious-metals exposure into this week's Asia open.

items.headline: Iran's oil minister Mohsen Paknejad resigns; NIOC chief named acting minister
items.summary: Iranian state media reported Paknejad's resignation "for personal reasons" amid the ongoing seven-month US-Iran conflict that has pressured Iran's economy. Hamid Bovard, CEO of the National Iranian Oil Company, was named acting oil minister.
items.actionable: Signals continued instability inside Iran's oil apparatus during an active regional escalation -- another marginal support for the oil/gold risk premium this week.

items.headline: Oil prices flat-to-down into Sunday reopen despite Hormuz/Yemen escalation
items.summary: WTI traded around $91.06-91.14/bbl and Brent near $102.25, both roughly flat to slightly lower, even as the Hormuz explosion and Yemen offensive headlines broke the same day -- suggesting much of the regional risk premium was already priced in.
items.actionable: Muted price reaction to fresh escalation suggests oil's risk premium is largely priced in; a sharp break higher would need a genuine supply disruption, not just headline risk.

items.headline: Gold and silver miner ETFs post second straight losing week as yields bite
items.summary: GDX fell 5.48%, GDXJ 6.16%, and SILJ 6.81% over the week ending Friday Oct 2 as the 10-year Treasury yield rose toward a 24-year high near 5.3%, raising the opportunity cost of holding precious metals despite a shockingly weak jobs report. Gold closed Friday at $4,162.30 (-3.68% weekly) after spiking intraday to roughly $4,259 and giving it back.
items.actionable: The portfolio's levered miner ETFs are in a two-week drawdown -- treat $4,143 gold as the near-term line in the sand before adding exposure; a break risks a deeper pullback toward $4,000.

items.headline: Silver slips to $60.37 at Fibonacci "golden pocket"; COMEX registered inventory keeps shrinking
items.summary: Silver fell about 5% on the week to close Friday at $60.37/oz as the 10-year yield hit 5.28% (highest since 2002) and the dollar index rose 0.9%. Separately, COMEX registered (deliverable) silver stood at 101.1M oz versus 236.5M oz eligible as of early October, with registered stock continuing a slow decline that keeps the delivery-tightness/backwardation narrative alive.
items.actionable: A hold above $58.04 keeps SLV/physical silver's uptrend intact; continued registered-inventory declines would be the bullish trigger to watch for re-adding exposure this week.

items.headline: Hang Seng tumbles 2.6% to 23,972 on reopen; Tencent and Xiaomi lead tech lower, Stock Connect dark to Oct 8
items.summary: Hong Kong's benchmark fell 640.98 points (-2.6%), its steepest one-day drop since March, on its first session back from the National Day holiday. Tencent lost over 2% and Xiaomi closed down 3.96% in a broad large-cap tech selloff; Stock Connect stays suspended until mainland exchanges reopen Thursday Oct 8, removing mainland buying support.
items.actionable: HK tech holdings face a liquidity-light week with no Stock Connect flow until Thursday -- expect wider swings and less dip-buying support into the open.

items.headline: Tencent signs $7bn deal to lease 100,000 Nvidia-class AI chips from Oracle
items.summary: Tencent's largest-ever overseas lease agreement gives it access to advanced AI chips via Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia over five years (~30% paid upfront), working around US export restrictions that block direct high-end chip purchases into China. Capital supports Tencent's Hunyuan AI models as it competes with DeepSeek and Alibaba.
items.actionable: Bullish for Tencent's AI-capex narrative and evidence that chip-export workarounds are scaling -- supports holding 0700.HK through the Friday selloff.

items.headline: CityDev's Lucerne Grand sells 61% of units on launch weekend
items.summary: CDL sold 350 of 570 units (61.4%) at Lucerne Grand (Lakeside Drive, Jurong) at an average S$2,480 psf over the Oct 3-4 launch weekend. Two-bedders led take-up at 65% sold, followed by three-bedders (62%) and premium four-bed units (51%).
items.actionable: Strong sell-through at a benchmark Jurong launch is a positive demand read-through for CityDev's residential pipeline, partly offsetting this month's strategic-overhaul-driven selloff.

items.headline: CityDev unveils S$6bn divestment plan, shares tumble 14.8% on the week
items.summary: CDL announced a 3-year (FY2027-29) plan to divest S$6bn of assets (commercial, hotels, legacy residential) while redeploying S$5bn roughly 60% to Singapore and 30% to China/Japan, retreating from Australia. Shares fell 8.1% on Sep 28 to S$7.59 -- the STI's worst performer that day -- and ended the week down 14.8%.
items.actionable: The strategic overhaul is the single biggest driver of this month's CityDev weakness -- expect continued volatility as divestment/redeployment details firm up over FY2027-29.

items.headline: Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust posts weaker quarter; DPU down 2.5%
items.summary: MPACT fell 1.65% to S$1.19 on Oct 2, about 21% below its 52-week high. Quarterly gross revenue fell 5.6% y/y to S$206.5m and NPI fell 6.8% to S$154.8m (Singapore NPI, 66% of the total, rose 1.0%), while DPU fell 2.5% y/y to S$0.0196; an analyst trimmed its target from S$1.52 to S$1.47.
items.actionable: Weakening ex-Singapore NPI and falling DPU argue for caution on the Mapletree PACT position while the 10Y yield stays near 24-year highs and refinancing costs bite.

items.headline: SGX cuts board lot sizes for DBS, UOB, OCBC and eight other blue chips from Oct 5
items.summary: From Monday Oct 5, 2026, SGX reduces the standard board lot from 100 shares to 10 shares (or 1 unit above S$100) for 11 higher-priced counters including DBS, UOB, OCBC, Keppel, Jardine Matheson/C&C, Great Eastern, Haw Par, Prudential, SGX itself and Venture -- cutting a DBS lot's minimum ticket from roughly S$7,760 to S$776 at early-September prices.
items.actionable: Lower minimum lot sizes should improve retail liquidity and could modestly support trading volumes in the portfolio's core DBS/UOB/OCBC holdings starting today.

items.headline: Lynas Rare Earths to acquire Meteoric Resources for ~A$968M, gaining Brazil heavy rare earth deposit
items.summary: Lynas announced an all-share deal for Meteoric's Caldeira project in Brazil, raising measured+indicated resources ~79% and giving Lynas its own feedstock for heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium) outside China. Lynas shares fell nearly 9% on dilution/financing concerns while Meteoric surged 47%; close expected March 2027 pending Brazilian regulatory and shareholder approval.
items.actionable: Near-term negative for Lynas on dilution risk, but strategically bullish for the non-China rare-earth diversification thesis underlying the watchlist -- a dip worth monitoring if execution risk proves manageable.

items.headline: China's suspended rare-earth export-control expansion set to lapse Nov 10, 2026
items.summary: China's Oct 2025 extraterritorial export-control expansion (covering foreign products with >=0.1% Chinese-origin rare-earth content) remains under a one-year truce from the Trump-Xi Busan meeting that expires Nov 10, 2026 -- 52 days before a US DFARS defense-procurement ban takes effect. Analysts see three scenarios: truce extension, selective licensing, or full reimposition with extraterritorial reach.
items.actionable: Nov 10 is the key catalyst date for the rare-earths watchlist this quarter -- a truce extension would be a relief-rally trigger for MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels, while reimposition would be a bullish shock for Western-aligned names.
